record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: Can stationary three-dimensional Einstein-Vlasov solutions be found whose spatial density resembles realistic disk galaxies, meaning solutions with a density core as close to planar and as extremely flattened as observed disk galaxies, despite current constructed oblate spheroidal and rotating solutions not satisfactorily resembling such galaxies?

evidence.quote: Given the prevalence of disk galaxies in the observable universe, it is reasonable to ask whether such a morphology is represented in the space of stationary solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system.

There exist models of disk galaxies which are confined to the plane, cf. e.g. [40, 18], but it would be desirable to obtain three-dimensional solutions which are disk-like in the sense that the core of the density is as close to planar as possible.

In conclusion, our solutions do not satisfyingly resemble the extremely flattened galaxies which are observed in nature. We find it to be a central open problem to answer the question whether or not it is possible to obtain solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system which resemble realistic disk galaxies.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Vlasov system in general relativity, which couples Einstein's field equations to the collisionless Vlasov (kinetic) equation for a phase-space distribution function f = f(x,p) ≥ 0 on the tangent bundle of a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime (M,g). The matter is described by the energy-momentum tensor

  T_{μν}(x) = ∫ f(x,p) p_μ p_ν (−det g)^{−1/2} d^4 p,

restricted to the mass shell g^{μν} p_μ p_ν = −m^2, and f is constant along the geodesic flow. A stationary solution is a triple (M, g, f) admitting a timelike Killing vector field, with g asymptotically flat and the spatial matter density

  ρ(x) = T_{μν} n^μ n^ν

(where n is the unit normal to a stationary spacelike slice) compactly supported in the slice.

Question: Does there exist a stationary, asymptotically flat, axially symmetric solution (M, g, f) of the Einstein–Vlasov system whose three-dimensional spatial density ρ has a core that is highly flattened toward an equatorial plane — quantitatively, with the ratio of the vertical extent of the support of ρ (perpendicular to the symmetry axis) to its radial extent arbitrarily small, while ρ is not supported entirely in a two-dimensional plane — so as to resemble the morphology of an observed disk galaxy? Equivalently, can the family of stationary three-dimensional Einstein–Vlasov solutions include configurations whose density profile is as planar and as extremely oblate as observed disk galaxies, going beyond the mildly oblate spheroidal and rotating configurations currently known to exist?
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on stationary solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov system reports spherically symmetric static solutions, axially symmetric oblate spheroidal and rotating solutions, and (in 2022) axisymmetric bifurcations from Kerr. No construction of three-dimensional stationary Einstein–Vlasov solutions whose density core matches the extreme flattening of realistic disk galaxies has been reported; the question is identified as a central open problem and no resolution has been found in available sources.

status_evidence.title: The Einstein-Vlasov System/Kinetic Theory (Living Reviews)
status_evidence.snippet: Only static, spherically symmetric solutions have been constructed in the relativistic Einstein-Vlasov case, but stationary axially symmetric solutions have been found in the Newtonian Vlasov-Poisson case.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of stationary Einstein–Vlasov solutions to date are limited and do not include realistic flattened disk-galaxy morphologies.

status_evidence.title: Stationary axisymmetric Einstein-Vlasov bifurcations of the Kerr spacetime
status_evidence.snippet: A one-parameter family of stationary axisymmetric and asymptotically flat spacetimes solutions to the Einstein-Vlasov system bifurcating from the Kerr spacetime.
status_evidence.claim: Recent axisymmetric stationary Einstein–Vlasov constructions exist but do not address extreme disk-like flattening.
